title: Optimize quantized kernels (INT8/FP8) + smoothquant and dequant fusion; scheduler + KV-cache batching improvements
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: reduce per-token latency and increase throughput for quantized models (INT8/FP8) by optimizing low-level kernels and fusion paths, and by making scheduling/KV-cache batching aware of quantization shapes. This PR introduces: 1) a fused dequant->matmul path for common FP8->INT8 serving flows to avoid extra memory copies and reduce dequant overhead; 2) smoothquant-aware scaling integration so kernels apply per-channel rescaling inline with matmul/fused ops; 3) microkernel changes with improved memory layout and vectorized paths for INT8/FP8 on NVIDIA Ampere and Ada architectures; 4) scheduler hints so continuous batching prioritizes requests with compatible sequence-length/quant-profile to improve batching efficiency; 5) KV-cache packing changes that avoid extra re-quantization during cache writes and reads. The changes are backward-compatible: models without quantization follow the existing code paths. Performance summary (microbenchmarks): - FP8/INT8 end-to-end generation latency reduced by 12-28% depending on sequence length and batch composition; - Token throughput improved by up to 1.6x for heavily quantized models with mixed-length batching; - GPU memory transient allocation decreased by ~15% due to fused paths and fewer scratch buffers. Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests added - [x] Scheduler changes with unit/integration tests - [x] KV-cache packing tests and regression suite - [x] Microbench harness updated (perf/benchmarks/quant-kernels) - [x] Release notes entry drafted - [x] Verified on internal canary fleet (redwood-perf-canary) Refs: ENG-2345 (quant perf epic), design doc: /docs/design/quant-fusion.md, earlier PRs: pr-998877, pr-142837. How to test locally: run `bazel test //runtime/quant:all` then `python perf/benchmarks/quant_bench.py --config=fp8-int8 --model=gpt-medium --runs=50`.

review_comments: Jonas Meyer: Great direction. Two questions: (1) are the fused paths safe for mixed-precision models that selectively use fp32 in attention? (2) what's the fallback cost when the fused kernel isn't available?

Ava Chen: Answered - we detect mixed-precision at dispatch and route to the existing fp32 path; fallback cost measured ~1.8ms per batch on our medium model (not significant for large batch sizes). Added a unit test to cover dispatch fallback.
Priya Shah: Can we expose a per-model flag to turn off the scheduler affinity if users want deterministic routing?
Ava Chen: Added config option runtime.scheduler.quant_affinity=false and documented it. Default remains enabled for perf.
Marcus Li (LGTM): Verified perf numbers on canary (nightly run 2025-02-25). Please squash commits and add release note.
